clips.text: Let's be honest. Nobody reads the docs. Not the read me, not the wiki, and definitely not the change log. So here's a cartoon instead.
This is pixel reel. Give it a list of scenes, and it plays them back as a narrated pixel art video, right in your browser. No video editor. No timeline. No progress bar stuck at ninety nine percent.
A reel is one small file with a list of scenes. Each scene has a title, a caption, the words to say, and a picture. That's it. Your shopping list is more complicated.
Pictures are drawn in code, with a little pixel kit. Sprites. Parallax. Typewriter text. And, most importantly, confetti.
Can't draw? Same. Pick a ready-made picture, like a list, a terminal or a chat, and just fill in the words.
This voice was recorded offline by Kokoro, an open speech model. No cloud, no A P I key, no subscription. Don't fancy me? Pick another voice, or plug in any speech engine.
No recording yet? Your browser reads it out instead, like a satnav having a moment, so a brand new reel plays straight away.
Captions type along as I talk. Pause me, skip me, drag me back and forth, or switch me off entirely. Rude, but fine.
Scenes can fade, wipe, dissolve, slide, or close with an iris, like an old cartoon. There's also a star wipe. We're not proud of it.
Where does it help? Onboarding new starters. Release notes people actually watch. Walking a reviewer through a pull request. School lessons that keep the back row awake.
Pitch decks. Game trailers. Status updates for a boss who won't read a document, but will absolutely watch a cartoon. And change logs, finally seen by human eyes.
It's just static files, so it goes anywhere: GitHub Pages, any web host, or an animated banner in your read me. Like the one you probably clicked to get here.
Scenes are just data, so robots can write them too. Turn release notes into a reel in one command, have C I make one for every release, or let an A I agent do the lot. No pay rise required.
Making your own takes about a minute. Clone it, start it, make a reel, record the voices. That's it. The hardest part is deciding what to explain.
That's pixel reel. Thanks for watching to the very end, which is more than anyone has ever done for a read me. Now go and explain something.
